html:
The Odawa, or Ottawa, are an Anishinaabe people of the upper Great Lakes, living around Georgian Bay, Manitoulin Island and northern Michigan. Their name is often explained as "traders", and they were known as middlemen in the trade between the lakes and the St. Lawrence.

They speak a form of the Anishinaabe language and, with the Ojibwe and Potawatomi, make up the Council of Three Fires. They grew maize, fished and carried furs by canoe to New France, whose close allies they were in the fur trade. After the Iroquois wars of the mid 1600s scattered them, many settled at Michilimackinac and later at L'Arbre Croche in Michigan. In 1763 the Odawa leader Pontiac led a rising against the British, Pontiac's War. Today Odawa communities live in Michigan, Ontario (notably at Wiikwemkoong on Manitoulin) and Oklahoma. The wider homeland appears on the map as Anishinabewaki.
